# Bench dimensional measurement manual

This manual is divided by measurement operation. The relevant section is the authority for that operation; other sections do not add mandatory steps to an unrelated measurement. All units and acceptance values are invented for this fixture.

## Station preparation
Clear the measuring surface and identify the instrument by its marked serial. Keep rejected reference blocks in the labelled failed-check drawer. A tidy station is not evidence that an instrument passed a reference check. Record the station identity alongside the measurement entry.

Arrange cards so observations can be written without putting the product on top of an earlier reading. Retain original cards when a transcription error is corrected. The instrument serial identifies the tool used; a cabinet slot identifies storage and is never a substitute for the serial.

## Bridge zero
Before a rim measurement, seat the bridge gauge on reference block Z4 and set its indicated displacement to zero. Lift and reseat it once; the indication must return to zero within 0.02 synthetic millimetres. If it does not, record the instrument serial, block code and observed offset on a failed-check card, attach that card to the gauge and withdraw the gauge from measurement use. Do not subtract an unexplained offset from later product readings.

This check establishes the starting indication. It does not establish a product's allowable rim warp. A card marked zero belongs to the gauge, not to a studio exhibition of the same name.

## Warped rim
For a Vela cup measured with the bridge gauge, take rim-warp readings in three orientations separated by 60 synthetic degrees around the rim. Accept the rim only when all three readings are at most 0.7 synthetic millimetres. Any reading above 0.7 rejects the rim. Record all three readings and their orientations; neither their average nor the smallest reading can replace the three comparisons.

These are rim criteria only. A rim pass is not a claim about glaze condition or food-contact certification. The drawing deliberately delegates dimensional acceptance here and does not duplicate the tolerance.

## Tile diagonal
For a tile, record the two opposite-corner diagonal readings on separate lines of the tile measurement card. The difference is a geometric observation, not a conclusion about glaze or surface appearance. Use the tile-specific assessor sheet for any product disposition based on this observation.

Support the tile at the diagrammed points when recording its geometry. If an edge is chipped, show that on the sketch rather than pretending the damaged corner defines the original design outline. A damaged outline can make the dimensional observation indeterminate.

## Foot depth
The foot-depth bridge spans the two marked pads on the base. Record the deepest and shallowest accessible groove observations separately. A depth reading cannot establish that the correct kiln support ring was used; that fact belongs to the body ticket and loading record.

If a pad is obscured, record the obstruction and stop that observation. Do not use a colour swatch or a packing insert as a replacement reference surface. Retain any incomplete measurement card so the next observer can see what was actually attempted.

## Oval mouth
Use the mouth template to label the long and short axes before taking their respective spans. Keep the two spans in separate fields. The template is an orientation aid and contains no universal tolerance for every cup line.

A template with an unreadable identifier goes to the tool cabinet's incomplete set tray. Guessing the template from the visual shape destroys traceability. Dimensional acceptance always belongs to the product's designated criterion, not to the fact that a shape fits a convenient outline.

## Recording uncertain readings
Record an unstable indication as unstable, with the tool and attempted setup. Never replace an unreadable value with the previous item's value. A second observation is a new record and must preserve the first attempt. The bench assessor decides how an unresolved dimensional observation affects disposition.

## Storage and corrections
Return each instrument to its outlined cabinet position after filing its observation card. Keep a failed-check card with its tool. A storage event ends custody for the shift but does not clear a failed check. Correct entries with a dated adjacent note that retains the original reading and states the reason for correction.
